gaps.question: Which specific certifications (UL, FCC, DOE) are actually held per product family?
gaps.notes: Live infenergypower.com product page for the Black Warrior 1500W e-bike (SKU BW-1500W-60AH) states no UL/DOT/safety certification and instead carries an explicit legal disclaimer: 'Intended for off-road use or on private property. gaps.question: Should Infenergy adopt the founder's Shark Tank pitch framing (crisis/urgency language, 'Disaster Proof Products' naming, statistics like '92% of homes lack backup power'), or preserve the current calm, non-fear-based locked voice? These directly conflict.
gaps.reason_needed: Founder-authored Shark Tank pitch conflicts with locked brand voice and guardrails already established in founder_brand_manifesto.json.
gaps.downstream_impact: Determines whether future copy may reference crisis statistics or 'Disaster Proof' branding at all.
gaps.notes: Live-site evidence (infenergypower.com homepage, fetched this date) shows the business is CURRENTLY publishing urgency/crisis-adjacent framing in production already: hero copy 'WHEN THE LIGHTS GO OUT, WILL YOU BE READY?', 'Don't let unexpected outages leave you vulnerable', and a section literally headlined 'LIFE-SAVING POWER'. This directly contradicts the locked founder_brand_manifesto.json VoiceDNA.prohibited_phrases entry banning the phrase 'life-saving', and shows the calm-only voice is not being followed on the live storefront today. This is presented as evidence only, not a resolution — deliberately NOT auto-applied to the locked voice guardrails, because loosening the 'life-saving' prohibition carries potential product-liability/false-guarantee risk for power equipment and should get explicit owner sign-off rather than being inferred from what the site currently happens to say. Recommend the owner either (a) confirm the calm-voice guardrail is correct and have the live site copy updated to match, or (b) explicitly approve limited, non-absolute urgency framing (e.g. 'be ready' style) while keeping the strongest banned terms (SHTF, doomsday, panic, guaranteed, unbreakable) off-limits.
